note: Ps118 processional thanksgiving, closes the Hallel (29v). Read by CHAR-ARC. A antiphonal call GIVE-THANKS + let those who FEAR say his love endures v1-4; B deliverance+trust v5-9 (CALLED, will not FEAR, HATE, TAKE-REFUGE vs TRUST in man/princes); C surrounded-but-helped v10-14 (God's acts, no chars); D right-hand does valiantly v15-18 (RIGHTEOUS, LIVE not die, RECOUNT his deeds); E entrance liturgy v19-29 (GIVE-THANKS at the gates, RIGHTEOUS enter, THANK, MARVELOUS, REJOICE/GLAD, BLESSED/bless, GIVE-THANKS/EXTOL, GIVE-THANKS). God's good/steadfast-love/answered/helper/strength/right-hand/save = qualifiers; nations-surrounded/stone-cornerstone/festal-sacrifice imagery = standalone.

dims.v: paired with his enduring steadfast love
v1: 'Oh GIVE THANKS (yadah) to the LORD, for he is good' - the antiphonal call opening the processional psalm.
paired with confessing his enduring love
v4: 'Let those who FEAR (yare) the LORD say, His steadfast love endures forever' - the reverent joining the antiphon.
on the LORD out of distress
v5: 'Out of my distress I CALLED (qara) on the LORD' - the cry from the strait place, the turn to God that the answer follows.
paired with the LORD on his side
v6: 'The LORD is on my side; I will not FEAR (yare). What can man do to me?' - the fearlessness of the God-backed, dread dissolved by God's presence.
paired with the LORD his helper
v7: 'I shall look in triumph on those who HATE (sane) me' - the enemies' enmity, over which the God-helped psalmist prevails.
paired with the folly of trusting man
v8: 'It is better to TAKE REFUGE (chasah) in the LORD than to trust in man' - reliance on God preferred to reliance on man.
paired with taking refuge in God
v8: 'than to TRUST (batach) in man' - the misplaced confidence in man, weighed against refuge in God and found wanting.
paired with the folly of trusting princes
v9: 'It is better to TAKE REFUGE (chasah) in the LORD than to trust in princes' - reliance on God preferred to reliance on the powerful.
paired with taking refuge in God
v9: 'than to TRUST (batach) in princes' - the misplaced confidence in the mighty, against refuge in God.
paired with the songs in their tents
v15: 'Glad songs of salvation are in the tents of the RIGHTEOUS (tsaddiq)' - the just, whose homes ring with the joy of deliverance.
v17: 'I shall not die, but I shall LIVE (chayah), and recount the deeds of the LORD' - the resolve to live for testimony, life spared for praise.
paired with living to tell them
v17: 'and RECOUNT (saphar) the deeds of the LORD' - the testimony the spared life exists for, God's works declared.
paired with entering the gates of righteousness
v19: 'that I may enter through them and GIVE THANKS (yadah) to the LORD' - the thanksgiving that is the aim of entering the gates.
paired with entering the LORD's gate
v20: 'This is the gate of the LORD; the RIGHTEOUS (tsaddiq) shall enter through it' - the just who alone pass through God's gate.
paired with God's answer and salvation
v21: 'I THANK (yadah) you that you have answered me and have become my salvation' - the personal thanks for the deliverance.
v23: 'This is the LORD's doing; it is MARVELLOUS (pala) in our eyes' - the wonder of the people at God's reversal, amazement at his work.
in the day the LORD has made
v24: 'This is the day that the LORD has made; let us REJOICE (gil) and be glad in it' - the exultation of the festal assembly.
v24: 'let us rejoice and be GLAD (samach) in it' - the gladness of the day of salvation.
him who comes in the LORD's name
paired with blessing from the house of the LORD
v26: 'BLESSED (barak) is he who comes in the name of the LORD!' - the benediction on the one entering, the processional welcome.
from the house of the LORD
v26: 'We BLESS (barak) you from the house of the LORD' - the blessing spoken from the temple over the coming worshippers.
v28: 'You are my God, and I will GIVE THANKS (yadah) to you' - the personal thanksgiving to God as his own.
v28: 'you are my God; I will EXTOL (rum) you' - the lifting-up of God in worship.

v29: 'Oh GIVE THANKS (yadah) to the LORD, for he is good' - the closing antiphon, the psalm sealed as it began.
